title: Cohen–Macaulay groupoid slicing lowers orbit-fibre dimension by one

standard_prerequisites.name: Explicit prerequisite boundary

standard_prerequisites.use: Groupoid restriction and stabilizer base change, dimension of locally finite-type groupoids over a field, prime avoidance, dimension formula for Cohen–Macaulay local rings, and the standard flatness criterion for a fibrewise nonzerodivisor.

core_obligations: Identify the stabilizer dimension with the double fibre quotient and use d_2>d_1 to choose a hypersurface avoiding every minimal prime of the Cohen–Macaulay fibre.
Show the chosen slice preserves the required Cohen–Macaulay map and lowers the identity-fibre dimension by exactly one.

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the stabilizer dimension with the double fibre quotient and use d_2>d_1 to choose a hypersurface avoiding every minimal prime of the Cohen–Macaulay fibre.
Show the chosen slice preserves the required Cohen–Macaulay map and lowers the identity-fibre dimension by exactly one.

difficulty_reason: The key work is finding one equation compatible with both source and target and simultaneously preserving Cohen–Macaulayness while cutting fibre dimension. The double-fibre/stabilizer comparison is not supplied by prime avoidance alone; H2 is supported.
